name: application-alert-dialog
title: Alert Dialog
description: Blocking confirmation dialogs for destructive or consequential actions, built on the native dialog element with no dismiss-by-backdrop-click affordance.
useWhen: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action, such as deleting an account or record.
Interrupting the user to confirm they want to lose unsaved work before navigating away.
The user must make an explicit choice (confirm or cancel) before continuing — no implicit dismissal.
avoidWhen: The action is reversible or low-stakes — a toast with an undo action is less disruptive.
You need arbitrary content or a form inside the dialog — use a standard modal instead.
Dismissing by clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape without an explicit choice is acceptable for this action.
responsiveBehavior: The dialog is centered via the native dialog element's default UA styles and constrained to max-w-md; it stays comfortably readable down to small viewports without additional breakpoints.
accessibility: Built on the native <dialog> element opened with showModal(), which traps focus and blocks interaction with the rest of the page automatically.
aria-labelledby and aria-describedby point at the title and description so screen readers announce both when the dialog opens.
Unlike a general-purpose modal, this pattern intentionally omits closedby="any" — the user must choose Cancel or Confirm rather than dismiss via backdrop click.
The destructive action button uses a red focus ring to reinforce which action requires deliberate intent.
